## Root Cause Analysis

### Root Cause
The error occurred due to a DataIntegrityViolationException when attempting to insert a value into the 'NAME' column of the 'user' table. The value being inserted was a URL string that exceeded the maximum length of 255 characters allowed for the 'NAME' column, which is defined as CHARACTER VARYING(255). The exact SQL statement that caused the error was: 'insert into "user" (email,name,id) values (?,?,default)'. The input data causing the error was a URL string that was 744 characters long.

### Component Affected
The 'user' table in the database, specifically the 'NAME' column, which is defined as CHARACTER VARYING(255).

### Code/DB Fix
1. Update the database schema to increase the maximum length of the 'NAME' column to accommodate the longer URL string. For example, you can alter the column definition to CHARACTER VARYING(1000).
2. Update the application code to ensure that the URL string being inserted into the 'NAME' column does not exceed the new maximum length. This can be done by validating the input data before it is inserted into the database.

### Verification Steps
1. Verify that the database schema has been updated to increase the maximum length of the 'NAME' column.
2. Verify that the application code has been updated to validate the input data before it is inserted into the database.
3. Redeploy the updated application code and database schema to ensure that the changes are applied and the error is resolved.
